resorts.name: Sugar Bowl
resorts.productName: 4 x Young Adult (13-22) single-day lift ticket, Sunday-Friday online advance rate
resorts.youngAdultBand: Young Adult 13-22 $77/day Sun-Fri online (vs $89 for Adult 23-64) - age 21 qualifies, and it beats every announced pack
resorts.restrictions: Sunday-Friday non-holiday only at $77; Saturday/holiday is $90 Young Adult. Must buy ONLINE in advance - the Young Adult window rate is $149. $77 is a dynamic 'starting' rate that rises with demand, so only the earliest buyers get it. 26/27 tickets are NOT purchasable yet: 'Lift tickets, lessons and rentals for the 2026/27 season will become available for booking this fall.' The announced 26/27 multi-day packs are flat-rate with NO age band, so they are worse for a 21-year-old: Midweek Magic $89/day (Mon-Thu) = 3 days $267 + one $77 Young Adult Sun-Fri ticket = $344; Select 3-Pack $99/day (Sun-Fri non-holiday) = $297 + $77 = $374; Anytime 3-Pack $199/day = $597 + $77 = $674. Reserved Upper Lot parking is $35 extra on weekends and holidays.
resorts.quote: Youth (13-22) $77 $149 (Sunday-Friday, online / window); Young Adult (13-22) $90 $189 (Saturday + Holiday)

resorts.name: Donner Ski Ranch
resorts.productName: 3 x 'Old School Days' adult day ticket (Tue/Wed/Thu) + 1 x regular adult all-day ticket
resorts.youngAdultBand: none - Adult band is 18-69 and Youth is 13-17, so a 21-year-old pays the full adult rate
resorts.restrictions: LAST SEASON'S PRICES - the pricing page is still headed 'Pricing 2025 - 2026' and no 2026-27 day rates are published anywhere. Old School Days run Tuesday/Wednesday/Thursday ONLY, so at most 3 of the 4 days can be $69 and the 4th is a regular $119 all-day ticket (3 x $69 + $119 = $326). Four Old School days cannot fit inside one 5-night trip. NO online sales, NO reservations, NO multi-day packs - every ticket is sold in person at the window on the day of use. Lifts 9am-4pm, no night skiing. A 2026-27 adult season pass does exist (donnerskiranch.com/store is headed 'Donner Ski Ranch 2026-2027 Season Passes') but the storefront is a JavaScript SimpleTix widget and no price could be read off it, so no 26/27 pass figure is asserted here.
resorts.quote: Pricing 2025 - 2026 | Adult (18-69): All Day $119, Half Day $99, Old School Days $69. 'Old School Days will take place on Tuesdays, Wednesdays, and Thursdays starting January 6, 2026, except for February 17, 18, and 19, 2026.'

resorts.name: Tahoe Donner (Downhill)
resorts.productName: Adult (18-59) Unrestricted downhill season pass, public (non-member) rate
resorts.youngAdultBand: none - Junior is 7-17 and Adult is 18-59; no young adult, college or student tier exists
resorts.restrictions: This season pass is the ONLY published product that covers 4 days, and at $169/day it is almost certainly NOT the real cheapest route - Tahoe Donner publishes no public day-ticket dollar amount for 2026-27 OR 2025-26. Day tickets are dynamically priced and the only figure on the page is the member floor: 'Members always receive the best prices, starting at $55 per day for adults', plus 'advanced purchase discounts of up to 25% off the window rate'. Members are Tahoe Donner property owners; a San Jose group pays the unpublished public rate, and guest (member-accompanied) rates are day-of only and require a member present. The pass itself is unrestricted with no blackouts; 26/27 peak holiday periods are Dec 26 2026 - Jan 2 2027, Jan 16-18 2027 and Feb 13-20 2027. Pass prices already rose on Aug 18, 2026.

resorts.name: Mt. Rose Ski Tahoe
resorts.youngAdultBand: none - Mt. Rose has only Adult (16+) and Child (6-15). No young adult, college or student band appears on the season pass, lift ticket or daily specials pages.
resorts.restrictions: MIDWEEK-SAFE BUT EXPENSIVE, AND PROBABLY NOT THE REAL CHEAPEST. Mt. Rose publishes NO 2026-27 day-ticket price - pricing is fully dynamic and its own lift-ticket page carries only '(2024/25 Full price tickets $189 Adults/$95 Kids)', a two-season-old window rate. There is no 2025-26 day rate on any Mt. Rose page, so the cheapest 4-day route sourceable to the resort is a season pass. Off-Peak void dates: Nov 27-28, Dec 18 - Jan 2, Jan 16-17, Feb 13-15, PLUS every Saturday and Sunday in January and February, so a Jan/Feb trip must run Mon-Fri. The cheaper $375 Select Pass is NOT usable for this trip: it grants access on ONE self-chosen non-weekend day per week, covering only 1 day of a single 5-night trip. Mt. Rose has NO multi-pack, 4-pack or punch card - verified absent across the lift-tickets, daily-specials and season-passes pages. Standing daily specials exist but none delivers 4 days and the page carries no season year: Two'fer Tuesday (2 adult full-day tickets for the price of 1, non-holiday Tuesdays), Ladies Day Thursday $79 (women only), Active Military $79, Veterans $109, same-day-flyer $79.
resorts.quote: Off-Peak Pass - 'A full season pass with voided weekends during PEAK months (Jan & Feb)' - Adult (16+): $675

resorts.name: Sierra-at-Tahoe
resorts.youngAdultBand: Young Adult 13-22 exists and a 21-year-old qualifies: Unlimited $529 (vs $659 adult), Play $489 (vs $539 adult), Weekday $409 (same as adult). A separate 'College Student' Unlimited tier is also $529.
resorts.restrictions: MIDWEEK ONLY - 'Valid Monday-Friday, with blackouts. Blackout Dates: Every Saturday + Sunday, as well as Dec. 26-30, 2026 | Jan. 16-17, 2027 | Feb. 13-14, 2027.' Sierra has published NO 2026-27 day ticket and NO 2026-27 multi-pack: '2025/26 lift ticket products are no longer available for purchase. Stay tuned for more information on 2026/27 season lift ticket products.' The 3-PAK was killed a season ago: 'While still valid for use through the close of the season, 3-PAK products are no longer available to purchase for the 2025/26 season.' Last season's equivalent 4-day build lands on exactly the same number: 2025-26 Young Adult 3-PAK $88/day ($264 for 3 days) plus one 2025-26 Young Adult non-peak day ticket $145 = $409. If the group wants weekends, the next step up is the Play Pass at $489 Young Adult ($122.25/day) or Unlimited at $529 ($132.25/day).

notes: FIELD CONVENTION: packDays = 0 means the product is a season pass (unlimited visits), not a fixed-count pack. RANKING for a 21-year-old getting 4 full days: Sugar Bowl $308 ($77/day, 2026-27, Sun-Fri online) < Donner Ski Ranch $326 ($81.50/day, LAST SEASON'S prices, 3 midweek + 1 regular) < Sierra-at-Tahoe $409 ($102.25/day, 2026-27, midweek-only season pass) < Mt. Rose $675 < Tahoe Donner $676. TWO OF THESE FIGURES ARE SOFT AND MUST BE CAPTIONED AS SUCH ON THE SITE: Mt. Rose and Tahoe Donner both publish NO public day-ticket price for either 2026-27 or 2025-26, so their $675/$676 numbers are season passes - the only 4-day-capable products either resort actually prices. Once their day tickets load in fall 2026 both will very likely land far below $169/day. (A third-party aggregator, OnTheSnow, lists a 2025-26 Mt. Rose weekday adult rate of $119 and describes Tahoe Donner as dynamically priced with no figure at all; neither was treated as resort-sourced and neither is used in the numbers above.) ONLY DONNER SKI RANCH FALLS BACK TO LAST SEASON - its pricing page is still literally headed 'Pricing 2025 - 2026'. AGE 21 MATTERS AT ONLY TWO OF THE FIVE: Sugar Bowl's Young Adult 13-22 band ($77 vs $89 on day tickets) and Sierra's Young Adult 13-22 / College bands ($529 vs $659 Unlimited, $489 vs $539 Play, though the Weekday Pass is $409 either way). Donner Ski Ranch (adult 18-69), Tahoe Donner (adult 18-59) and Mt. Rose (adult 16+) have no 18-25 tier at all. NOTHING IS PURCHASABLE TODAY EXCEPT SEASON PASSES: Sugar Bowl says day tickets and packs 'will become available for booking this fall', Sierra says the same, Mt. Rose and Tahoe Donner day tickets are dynamic and unpriced, and Donner Ski Ranch never sells tickets in advance at all. Re-run this sweep in Oct/Nov 2026. SUGAR BOWL PACK CAVEAT: the $199 / $99 / $89-per-day Anytime, Select and Midweek Magic packs come from Sugar Bowl's own July 1 2026 article (sugarbowl.com/18806) and are echoed on sugarbowl.com/deals as 'Ski + Ride for $89/Day' via '3-Pack or Midweek ticket options', but shop.sugarbowl.com returns HTTP 403 and sugarbowl.com/3pack returns 404, so no pack price is confirmed against a live checkout and no pack is known to carry a Young Adult discount. GROUP HACKS FOR 8 PEOPLE, all confirmed 2026-27 on sierraattahoe.com/season-pass-benefits/: Sierra buddy tickets are $89 peak / $79 non-peak, passholders park free, and parking is otherwise $25/day but free for any car carrying 4 or more. Buddy allocations are Unlimited = unlimited with a max of 2 redemptions per day, Play = 12 for the season, Weekday = 10. Three people buying the $409 Weekday Pass unlock 30 buddy tickets, enough to cover the other five friends for all 4 days at $79 each - roughly $351 per person, about $88/day across the whole party, cheaper than eight Weekday Passes - but it is midweek-only and it could not be confirmed whether a Weekday passholder's buddy tickets carry weekend access. DONNER SKI RANCH'S REAL RISK IS LOGISTICS, NOT PRICE: window-only, day-of, no reservations, no advance purchase, and rentals are first-come first-served. For 8 people that means arriving early with no guarantee of gear. Groups of 20 or more get 10% off with 5 days' notice, so a party of 8 does not qualify. FOR REFERENCE, the prior sweep's benchmark - Boreal's iRide 4-Pack at $239, $59.75/day, no blackouts, confirmed 2026-27, price rises after 10/1/2026 - still beats all five of these resorts.
